title: Define variant compatibility matrix, automated gating tests, and pin semantics for open-model onboarding
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Background:
We continue to onboard community/open models into the Model Catalog. Recent onboarding runs surfaced ambiguity about which model artifacts (quantized variants, compile targets, and tokenizers) are considered 'compatible' with Redwood runtime variants, and how version pinning should behave when a model owner uploads multiple variants. This ticket clarifies the required compatibility matrix, the automated gating tests that must pass before a model is listed, and the semantics for explicit and automatic pinning.

Problem:
- Onboarding engineers and model authors make inconsistent assumptions about what 'supported' means (runtime, sequence length, quantization format, KV cache shape).
- Product and Console UX currently show a single version without clear pin semantics. Customers are confused when a model silently rolls to a new compilation or quantization variant.
- Lack of automated gating leads to regressions discovered only in production or in downstream customer tests.

Goal:
- Produce a one-page compatibility matrix that enumerates required metadata fields and a mapping to Redwood runtime families (e.g., rwd-gpt-a100-ot, rwd-gpt-gpu-quantized).
- Define automated gating tests (unit + integration) that validate a model artifact against runtime compatibility signals (tokenizer roundtrip, basic generation sanity, KV-cache correctness for seq lengths up to default limit).
- Specify pinning semantics: what 'pin to exact artifact', 'pin to major-model-version', and 'follow-latest-compile' mean in Console and API, and the defaults for community models.

Proposed approach:
1) Compatibility matrix: author a canonical CSV/Markdown that lists required artifact attributes (model_arch, weights_format, quantization_scheme, transformer_config hashes, tokenizer_id, supported_seq_lengths, memory_profile) and acceptable runtime families. This will be the single source of truth referenced by onboarding automation.
2) Automated gating tests: a runnable suite (python) executed by onboarding pipeline that emits pass/fail and a short JSON report. Tests include tokenizer roundtrip, short-context generation (prompt -> output length sanity), kv-cache consistency check (replay past tokens), and perf smoke (cold-start latency threshold).
3) Pin semantics: add three explicit pin modes in PRD/UI/API: EXACT, MAJOR, and FOLLOW_COMPILE. Default for community-open uploads is MAJOR. Document rollback and fallback behaviors when a pinned artifact becomes unavailable.

Out of scope:
- Changes to Dedicated capacity autoscaling policies.
- Deep performance tuning of kernels for specific models (this ticket only flags failures).

Dependencies:
- ENG-2314 (onboarding pipeline move to runner-v2)
- PM-9123 (prior compatibility work; reference but not duplicate)

Deliverables:
- compatibility-matrix.md (confluence link)
- gating-test-suite repo or folder with README and CI integration
- PRD section with exact Console strings and API contract for pin parameter
- Acceptance criteria checklist (below)
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix published in Confluence: lists artifact attributes, required fields, and mapping to runtime families
Gating test suite integrated into onboarding CI: a failed gate blocks publish; passes emit machine-readable report
Console shows explicit Pin Mode with three options (EXACT, MAJOR, FOLLOW_COMPILE) and the default is MAJOR for community uploads
REST API accepts optional 'pin_mode' and 'pin_reference' params; backend validation rejects inconsistent pin_reference with a clear error
Onboarding UX and API docs updated with examples and recommended defaults
Rollback/fallback policy documented: when pinned artifact missing, system will return a 409 with guidance; admins can configure auto-fallback to FOLLOW_COMPILE
At least 2 model onboarding test cases (one quantized, one fp16) exercise the gating suite end-to-end and are recorded in onboarding run logs
